mainTopic: A locked-away עירוב with a lost key, and an עירוב that is lost or ruined before or after nightfall
overview: The גמרא first fixes the wording of the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא). An עירוב locked in a cupboard with a lost key is valid on יום טוב but not on שבת. The fixed משנה also records a dispute about where the key turns up, in the city or in a field, which the גמרא explains with רבי שמעון's rule about one domain. רבה and רב יוסף instead explain the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר as a question of whether a wooden cupboard is a כלי or an אהל. They try to prove this from a משנה about a זב knocking on a cupboard. אביי rejects that proof, so אביי and רבא explain the case as a lock tied with a rope that must be cut with a knife. On that reading, the dispute depends on רבי יוסי and רבי נחמיה's rules about moving כלים on שבת. A new משנה then teaches that an עירוב lost or ruined before dark fails, but one ruined after dark still works, and it records a dispute about a doubtful case. The גמרא narrows the rolled-away case to four אמות, explains the pile-of-stones case so that it fits רבי, and shows why both cases are needed. It then begins explaining why the burnt and impure-תרומה cases are both listed, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: יום טוב versus שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves an earlier difficulty by saying the משנה is incomplete. It restates the first part: a locked-away עירוב with a lost key is valid on יום טוב but not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means to teach: If someone put his עירוב in a cupboard, locked it, and lost the key, it is still a valid עירוב. When is that true? On יום טוב. But on שבת, his עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier question by adding missing words to the משנה. It explains that the lenient ruling about the lost key applies only on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must be reachable at the start of the day. On יום טוב more actions are permitted, so the food still counts as reachable even without the key. On שבת those actions are forbidden, so the food is cut off and the עירוב fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words. The גמרא fills them in to explain the משנה.
A cupboard or tall cabinet
A key
Here, an עירוב תחומין: food placed to set a person's 'home base' for walking on שבת or יום טוב
In what case was this said? This phrase limits a ruling to a specific situation.

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'נתנו במגדל... הרי זה עירוב' are not the גמרא's own new ruling. They are the גמרא's rewritten, expanded version of the משנה.

phrases.english: It is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
If he placed it in a cupboard,
and locked it, and the key was lost —
it is a valid eiruv.
In what case is this said?
On a Festival,
but on Shabbat —
his eiruv is not a valid eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised on the משנה on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא (textual emendation of the משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the עירוב is always valid even though the key is lost
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency applies only on יום טוב. On שבת the עירוב is invalid.

steps.title: Where the key is found: city or field
steps.stepSummary: The rewritten משנה continues with a dispute. The תנא קמא says the עירוב is invalid whether the key is found in the city or the field. רבי אליעזר says it is valid in the city and invalid in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the key turns up, whether in the city or in a field, the עירוב is not valid. רבי אליעזר says: if it is in the city, the עירוב is valid. If it is in a field, the עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still the גמרא's rewritten version of the משנה. It now records a dispute about where the key is located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the key could be brought to the cupboard. If it could, the food is reachable and the עירוב works. The תנא קמא is strict in both places. רבי אליעזר treats the city differently from the field. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: It was found, or it turned out to be
In the city, a settled and enclosed area
In the field, an open area
The תנא who disagrees and is lenient about a key found in the city

phrases.english: If the key was found,
whether in the city or in the field —
his eiruv is not a valid eiruv.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
In the city — his eiruv is valid;
in the field — his eiruv is not valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא הַמַּפְתֵּחַ, בֵּין בָּעִיר בֵּין בַּשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rewritten text of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The rewritten משנה contains a dispute about a key found in the city versus the field

steps.title: Explaining the city/field distinction: רבי שמעון versus the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's leniency in the city follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות are one domain for objects that rested there at the start of שבת. The strictness in the field follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the city it is valid' follows רבי שמעון. He said that roofs, courtyards and enclosed lots are all one domain for objects that were there when שבת began. 'In the field it is not valid' follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's two rulings. It ties each ruling to a known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the city, רבי שמעון lets objects move between roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות, so the key can be brought to the cupboard. In the field, the key sits in a כרמלית, and the רבנן forbid carrying it there. Since the key cannot be brought, the עירוב is not reachable.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who treats several private areas as one domain for vessels
Roofs
Courtyards
Enclosed lots that are not used for living in
One single domain
That 'rested' there, meaning they were located there when שבת began

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an עירוב depends on whether the food could be reached in a permitted way. The sugya measures that by the carrying rules for each domain.

phrases.english: In the city — his eiruv is valid,
in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said:
Roofs and courtyards alike
and enclosed lots alike —
they are one domain
for utensils that began Shabbat in them.
In the field his eiruv is not valid —
in accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעִיר — עֵירוּבוֹ עֵירוּב, כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's two rulings in Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each ruling to a known opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The city/field split follows רבי שמעון's domain rule in the city and the רבנן's rule in the field
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: the dispute is about whether the key can be brought, and that depends on the carrying rules of where it lies.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: a wooden cupboard, vessel or tent
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain the משנה differently. The case is a wooden cupboard. One opinion calls it a כלי, so breaking it open is permitted and the עירוב is valid. The other calls it an אהל, so breaking it open is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: we are dealing with a wooden cupboard. One חכם holds it is a vessel, and there is no 'building' or 'demolishing' with vessels. The other חכם holds it is like a tent, a structure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף give a new, separate explanation of what the תנאים argue about. This is not about the key at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cupboard is a כלי, the prohibitions of בונה and סותר do not apply. So one may break it open and reach the food, and the עירוב is valid. If it is an אהל, breaking it is forbidden סתירה, the food cannot be reached, and the עירוב is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Two אמוראים who give this explanation together
Both of them
A wooden cupboard
The prohibition of building does not apply to vessels
Demolishing, one of the forbidden labors on שבת
A tent or structure, treated like a building

steps.confusionAlert: 'מר סבר... ומר סבר' does not name the speakers. Per the explanation, the first מר is the תנא קמא (the עירוב is valid) and the second is רבי אליעזר (the עירוב is invalid).

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:
Here we are dealing with a wooden cupboard,
for one Sage holds: it is a utensil,
and there is no building with utensils
and there is no demolishing with utensils.
And the other Sage holds: it is a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the משנה's dispute instead of Steps 1–3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about bringing the key from different domains
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is whether a wooden cupboard is a כלי (may be broken open) or an אהל (may not)

steps.title: Linking to the dispute about a זב knocking on a cupboard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the vessel-or-tent question is the same as an earlier dispute among תנאים. If a זב knocks on a carriage, chest or cupboard, the תנא קמא says they become טמא. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון say they stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches the dispute of these תנאים, as we learned: if a זב knocked on a carriage, a chest or a cupboard, they are impure. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון say they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבה and רב יוסף's question already appears in an earlier מחלוקת about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב makes a כלי impure by moving it (היסט), but only something that counts as a כלי can receive טומאה. The תנא קמא, who calls them impure, treats a cupboard as a כלי. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון, who call them pure, treat it like an אהל or structure.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
He knocked or struck
A carriage or large wooden box-cart
A chest
Impure / they declare pure
A תנא who, with רבי שמעון, rules these items pure

steps.whatToRemember: Second approach (רבה and רב יוסף): the עירוב dispute rests on whether a large wooden cupboard is a כלי or an אהל. This is the same question as the טומאה dispute about a זב knocking on such items.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one conceptual question, whether something is a vessel or a structure, controls rulings in two very different areas: שבת and טומאה.

phrases.english: And it is the dispute of these tanna'im,
as we learned:
If he knocked upon a carriage,
a chest, or a cupboard — they are impure.
Rabbi Neḥemya and Rabbi Shimon declare them pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רבה and רב יוסף's vessel-or-tent question in an existing dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whether a cupboard is a כלי or an אהל is already a known dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a זב knocking on a שידה, תיבה or מגדל

steps.title: The proof is completed: they argue whether a cupboard is a vessel or a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 5. It suggests that the תנא קמא holds the carriage, chest and cupboard are a כלי, while רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון hold they are an אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One master holds it is a vessel, and the other master holds it is a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the point of the proof it brought in step 5. It says the תנאים who argued about the זב were really arguing about the same thing as רבה and רב יוסף: is a cupboard a כלי or an אהל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי can become טמא when a זב moves it, but an אהל cannot. So the תנא קמא, who says טמא, would hold it is a כלי. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון, who say טהור, would hold it is an אהל. This would show that the vessel-or-tent question, which רבה and רב יוסף used to explain the עירוב dispute, already divides תנאים elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that…?' A formula that presents a suggested proof
They disagree
A vessel or utensil, which can become טמא
A tent or structure, treated like a building and not like a vessel

phrases.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this:
One master holds it is a vessel,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא, who rules טמא

phrases.english: and the other master holds it is a tent.
phrases.notes: רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון, who rule טהור

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof introduced in step 5 by stating what the תנאים were arguing about.
steps.raayaObject: That the vessel-or-tent question about a cupboard (רבה and רב יוסף) is an older dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a זב knocking on a carriage, chest or cupboard (תנא קמא against רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון).

steps.title: אביי shows that for a זב, what matters is movement, not vessel or tent
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. He cites a ברייתא: a tent that moved is טמא, and a vessel that did not move is טהור. The rule is that movement from the זב's own force makes it טמא, and movement from vibration leaves it טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Do you really think so? Wasn't it taught: a tent that moved is impure, and a vessel that did not move is pure. And the end of that teaching says: if they moved, they are impure. This is the rule: if it moved because of his force, it is impure; if it moved because of vibration, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. He shows from a ברייתא that whether something is a vessel or a tent does not decide the טומאה of a זב at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a tent that moved is טמא and a vessel that did not move is טהור. So the deciding factor is whether the object moved, not what category it belongs to. The rule at the end adds that it must move from the זב's direct force, not from the ground shaking under it. That means the תנאים could not have been arguing about vessel versus tent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do you think so?' Introduces an objection to the previous idea
'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?'
Was moved or shifted
Because of his own direct force
Vibration or trembling, such as shaking that comes from the floor
'This is the rule.' A summarizing principle

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'a tent that moved is טמא' as saying a tent is now a vessel. The ברייתא is only showing that the result depends on movement, whatever the category.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And do you think so?
But wasn't it taught: a tent that moved is impure,
a vessel that did not move is pure.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: וְאִם הָיוּ נִיסּוֹטִין — טְמֵאִים,
phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches: and if they moved, they are impure,
This is the rule:
if it moved because of his force, it is impure,
if because of vibration, it is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof completed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים in the זב dispute argued about whether a cupboard is a כלי or an אהל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that a זב's טומאה depends on actual movement caused by his force, not on whether the object is a vessel or a tent.

steps.title: אביי's new explanation: they argue about shaking caused by the זב's own force
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that movement from the זב's force makes it טמא and movement from vibration leaves it טהור. The case is shaking caused by his own force. The תנא קמא says that counts as movement. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון say it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Everyone agrees that if it moved because of his force, it is impure, and if because of vibration, it is pure. Here we are dealing with vibration caused by his force, and this is what they argue about: one master holds it counts as movement, and the other holds it does not count as movement.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the old explanation, אביי gives a new reading of the זב dispute that fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is no longer about the object's category. The case is in-between: the זב hit the object itself, so it shook, but it was not actually moved from its place. The תנא קמא treats this shaking as movement, so it is טמא. רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון do not, so it is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Moving something. A זב makes things טמא this way even without touching them
'We are dealing with.' Defines the case

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the only תנאים source for the vessel-or-tent explanation of the משנה. That is why the גמרא now needs a new explanation of the locked עירוב.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הֶיסֵּט מֵחֲמַת כֹּחוֹ — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that moving because of his force makes it impure,
and because of vibration, it is pure.
And here we are dealing with vibration caused by his force,
phrases.notes: He struck the object itself, so it shook but did not move from its place.

phrases.english: and this is what they disagree about:
one master holds it counts as movement,
and the other master holds it does not count as movement.
phrases.notes: רבי נחמיה and רבי שמעון: טהור

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the proof, אביי gives a new reading of the משנה from step 5 (the זב dispute) that fits the ברייתא he cited in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) of the תנאים dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argued about whether a cupboard is a vessel or a tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argued about whether shaking caused by the זב's own force counts as movement.

steps.title: So how do we explain the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the cupboard explanation has lost its support, the גמרא asks what case the locked-עירוב משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה, how do we explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא is preparing to give a new explanation of the משנה about the locked-away עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב יוסף explained the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר as a vessel-or-tent question, and they tied it to the זב dispute. אביי reread that dispute as being about shaking, not about vessel versus tent. So the גמרא needs another way to explain why the תנא קמא says the locked עירוב is valid and רבי אליעזר says it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: We establish or explain the case of a source
Our משנה

phrases.english: And our mishna, how do we explain it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the side discussion about the זב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the משנה about the locked עירוב with a lost key is describing.

steps.title: אביי and רבא: a lock tied with a rope that needs a knife to cut
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both say the משנה is about a lock tied with a rope. Without the key, the rope must be cut with a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: We are dealing with a lock tied with a rope, and a knife is needed to cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a new case for the משנה. It is not about a cupboard. It is about a lock fastened with a rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the key is lost, the only way to reach the עירוב is to cut the rope with a knife. The dispute between the תנא קמא (valid) and רבי אליעזר (invalid) now depends on whether one may pick up a knife for this purpose on שבת. The next two steps explain each side. It no longer depends on the vessel-or-tent question.

keyTerms.meaning: A lock
A rope or cord
A knife
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: The cupboard (vessel-or-tent) explanation lost its support from the תנאים. אביי and רבא explain the משנה as a lock tied with a rope that must be cut with a knife.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both said:
We are dealing with a lock tied with a rope,
and a knife is needed to cut it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with a new case for the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about a lock tied with a rope, so reaching the עירוב requires cutting the rope with a knife.

steps.title: The first opinion follows רבי יוסי, so the knife may be used
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא, who says the locked-up עירוב is valid, holds like רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי says almost every כלי may be moved on שבת. So the person may pick up a knife and cut the rope around the lock.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds like רבי יוסי, who said: all utensils may be moved on שבת except a large saw and the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא says the עירוב is still valid even though the key is lost. He follows רבי יוסי's lenient view about moving utensils on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the lock is tied with a rope, and without the key you must cut the rope with a knife. Under רבי יוסי a knife may be moved on שבת even for a use other than cutting food. So the person can reach his עירוב, and it counts as available. Only very heavy work tools, like a big saw or a plow blade, are off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
May be moved or picked up (on שבת)
A large saw, a heavy work tool
The blade (spike) of a plow

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: The first tanna holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: all utensils may be moved on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִמַּסָּר הַגָּדוֹל וְיָתֵד שֶׁל מַחֲרֵישָׁה.
phrases.english: except for a large saw and the blade of a plow.
phrases.notes: These heavy tools are kept for serious work and are guarded from other uses, so they stay forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rope-lock case from step 10 and explains the lenient side of the argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא allows moving a knife to cut the rope, because he follows רבי יוסי that almost all כלים may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows רבי נחמיה, so the knife may not be used
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר, who says the locked-up עירוב is not valid, holds like רבי נחמיה. רבי נחמיה says a כלי may be moved only for its normal use. A knife's normal use is cutting food, not cutting a rope, so the person cannot reach his עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר holds like רבי נחמיה, who said: even a cloak, even a spoon, may be moved only for the purpose of their normal use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side. רבי אליעזר follows רבי נחמיה's strict view, so the rope may not be cut and the עירוב is out of reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה is strict even with everyday items like a cloak or a spoon. They may be moved only for what they are normally used for. Cutting a rope is not a knife's normal use, so the person cannot open the cupboard. An עירוב you cannot reach does not work, unless the key is in town and can be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak or garment
A spoon or ladle
For the purpose of their normal use

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument about the locked cupboard comes down to the laws of moving utensils on שבת. Following רבי יוסי, you may use a knife to cut the rope, so the עירוב works. Following רבי נחמיה, you may not, so the עירוב does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern the גמרא uses often. A dispute in one area of הלכה (here, עירוב) is explained as depending on a dispute in a different area (here, moving כלים on שבת).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi Nechemya,
who said: even a cloak, even a spoon,
may be moved only for the purpose of their normal use.
phrases.notes: So a knife may be moved only to cut food, not to cut a rope.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair started in step 11 by explaining the strict side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר does not allow the knife to be used on the rope, because he follows רבי נחמיה that כלים may be moved only for their normal use. So the עירוב is out of reach.

steps.title: New משנה: an עירוב lost or ruined before or after nightfall
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Something may happen to the עירוב: it rolls outside the תחום, a pile of stones falls on it, it burns, or it was תרומה and became טמא. If this happened while it was still day, the עירוב does not work. If it happened after dark, the עירוב works.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the עירוב rolled outside the תחום, or a pile fell on it, or it burned, or it was תרומה and became טמא: if this happened while it was still day, it is not an עירוב. If it happened after dark, it is an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new topic: what happens if the עירוב food is lost or ruined. The answer depends on whether this happened before or after nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב sets your שבת home at the moment שבת begins, around בין השמשות. If the food was already gone or unusable before that moment, there was nothing to set your home, so the עירוב fails. If it was fine when שבת began, the עירוב already did its job, and losing it afterward does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
It rolled away
The 2,000-אמה limit for walking on שבת
A pile (of stones or rubble)
While it was still day, before שבת began
After it got dark, once שבת had begun

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think an עירוב must last the whole of שבת. It only needs to be whole and reachable at the moment שבת begins. After that, it can be lost or eaten and still works.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If it rolled outside the Shabbat limit,
phrases.notes: Now the person may not walk to it, so it is out of reach.

phrases.english: a pile fell on it, or it was burned,
or it was teruma and became impure,
phrases.notes: Impure תרומה may not be eaten, so it is no longer usable food.

phrases.english: if this happened while it was still day, it is not an eiruv.
If it happened after dark, it is an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The locked-cupboard discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב must be whole and reachable at the start of שבת. If it was ruined before nightfall it does not work. If it was ruined after nightfall it works.

steps.title: If we don't know when it happened: the donkey-driver and camel-driver
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes we do not know whether the עירוב was ruined before or after dark. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say the person is a 'חמר גמל.' He is pulled in two directions, so he must be strict both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is uncertain, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say: this person is a donkey-driver and camel-driver.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers a case where we are unsure when the עירוב was ruined. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה give a strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey-driver walks behind his animal, and a camel-driver walks in front. One person doing both is pulled backward and forward at once. Here, we do not know whether his שבת home is in his town or at the עירוב. So he may walk only in the area that is within 2,000 אמות of both places. The משנה goes on (next) with other תנאים who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt or uncertain case
A donkey-driver and camel-driver: someone pulled in two directions, so he is restricted on both sides

steps.confusionAlert: 'חמר גמל' is not about animals at all. It is a picture of being stuck in two directions. He gets the strict result of both possible שבת homes, not the lenient result of either one.

phrases.english: If it is uncertain,
phrases.notes: We do not know whether it happened before or after dark.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say:
this person is a donkey-driver and camel-driver.
phrases.notes: He may walk only where both possible שבת homes allow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם סָפֵק, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case of doubt to the rule given in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unclear whether the עירוב was ruined before or after nightfall, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה rule strictly. The person is restricted to the area that is within the limits of both his town and his עירוב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון: A doubtful עירוב is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון disagree with רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. They rule that a ספק עירוב is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: An עירוב that is in doubt is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the argument from the last step. When we do not know if the עירוב was ruined before or after dark, these תנאים say the עירוב still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה said the person is a 'חמר גמל' and must be strict in both directions. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון disagree and are lenient. Since עירובי תחומין is a rabbinic law, a doubt about it is treated leniently.

keyTerms.meaning: An עירוב whose validity is in doubt. Here, we do not know if it was ruined before or after dark.
Valid; it works.
A תנא, here siding with רבי יוסי.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה (previous step) are strict: חמר גמל. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון (this step) are lenient: the עירוב is valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
A doubtful eruv is valid.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the 'חמר גמל' view in the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on a ספק עירוב.

steps.title: אבטולמוס testified that a doubtful עירוב is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי supports his lenient view with testimony. אבטולמוס reported in the name of five זקנים that a ספק עירוב is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: אבטולמוס testified in the name of five זקנים about a doubtful עירוב, that it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his ruling. He shows it is an old tradition from five earlier זקנים, not just his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the lenient view was a disagreement among תנאים. Now it carries the weight of testimony passed down from five earlier sages. This makes the lenient ruling stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage who passed on the tradition.
Testified; formally reported a received tradition.
Five Elders, earlier sages.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two views on a doubtful עירוב. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say חמר גמל, so be strict both ways. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say it is valid, backed by the testimony of five זקנים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
Avtolemos testified in the name of five Elders
about a doubtful eruv, that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives traditional support for the lenient ruling in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a ספק עירוב is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The testimony of אבטולמוס in the name of five זקנים.

steps.title: רבא: The עירוב fails only if it rolled more than four אמות away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רבא limits the משנה's rule about an עירוב that rolled outside the תחום. It only fails if it rolled more than four אמות past the edge, because the person who places an עירוב gets four אמות around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'It rolled outside the תחום.' רבא said: They only taught this when it rolled more than four אמות outside. But if it is within four אמות, it is still fine, because one who places his עירוב has four אמות around it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first case of the משנה, an עירוב that rolled outside the תחום. רבא explains that this is not as strict as it sounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is when the person put his עירוב right at the edge of his town's תחום. By placing it there, he makes that spot his home for שבת, and he gets four אמות around it. So if the עירוב rolled only up to four אמות outside, it is still within his reach, and the עירוב works.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here.
Rolled away.
The 2,000-אמה שבת boundary.
'They only taught this when...' A phrase that limits a rule to a narrower case.
Four cubits, the personal space a person has around his שבת spot.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic idea behind עירובי תחומין. Placing the עירוב makes that spot your שבת home, with four אמות of space around it like any person.

phrases.english: Gemara:
'It rolled outside the techum.'
Rava said:
They only taught this where it rolled
more than four cubits away,
but within four cubits, it is still valid,

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹתֵן עֵירוּבוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: because one who places his eruv has four cubits around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by narrowing the first case of the משנה from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב that rolled outside the תחום fails only if it went more than four אמות away. Within four אמות it is valid.

steps.title: Assumption: The person could still dig out the buried עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case of a pile of stones falling on the עירוב. At first it assumes the person could physically remove the stones and take the עירוב if he wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A pile fell on it' and so on. You might think that if he wanted, he could take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא makes a first assumption about the case of the stones, to prepare a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עירוב can be reached physically, the only thing stopping the person is a rabbinic rule. Stones are מוקצה, and moving them on שבת is forbidden only by the rabbis. Keep this in mind: the next question depends on this assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: A pile of stones.
'It would enter your mind.' A first assumption that may later be changed.
To take or pick up.

phrases.english: 'A pile fell on it,' and so on.
It would enter your mind
that if he wanted, he could take it out.
phrases.notes: The only problem is the rabbinic rule against moving stones, which are מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּאִי בָּעֵי מָצֵי שָׁקֵיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second case of the משנה and sets up an assumption for the coming challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: the buried עירוב can physically be reached. Only a rabbinic rule blocks it.

steps.title: Does the משנה disagree with רבי about rabbinic rules at twilight?
steps.stepSummary: Based on the assumption, the גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי. רבי says rabbinic decrees (שבות) do not apply during בין השמשות. So the person could remove the stones then, and the עירוב should be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי? Because if it were like רבי, he said: Anything forbidden only as a rabbinic decree was not decreed during twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem from the assumption in the last step. It suggests the משנה goes against the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב takes effect at בין השמשות. Moving מוקצה stones is only a שבות, and רבי says such rules do not apply during בין השמשות. So the person could have reached his עירוב at that moment, and it should be valid. Yet the משנה says it is not valid. Therefore the משנה seems to disagree with רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say...?' Suggests a possibly troubling conclusion.
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת, such as moving מוקצה.
Decreed; made a rabbinic rule.
Twilight, the uncertain time between day and night. This is when the עירוב takes effect.

steps.confusionAlert: The key is timing. The עירוב 'acquires' at בין השמשות. So what counts is whether the person could reach it then, not later on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a big problem if a משנה does not follow רבי, since he edited the משנה. The גמרא will look for a way to fit the משנה with his view.

phrases.english: Shall we say our Mishnah is not like Rebbi?
For if it were like Rebbi, he said:
anything forbidden only as a rabbinic decree,
they did not decree it during twilight.
phrases.notes: So the stones could be cleared at twilight, and the עירוב should be valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a challenge from the assumption in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that an עירוב buried under a pile of stones before dark is not valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the rabbinic rule of מוקצה blocks the person, then by רבי's rule that שבות does not apply at בין השמשות, he could take the עירוב at the moment it takes effect. So it should be valid, and the משנה would contradict רבי.

steps.title: The stones can only be removed with digging tools
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow רבי. It is talking about a case where getting the עירוב out requires a hoe and a spade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי, the ruling is only needed for a case where you would need a hoe and a spade to get the עירוב out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 19. It says the משנה can follow רבי after all, because the case is one where the stones can only be removed by digging with tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי only said that a שבות (a rabbinic decree) does not apply during בין השמשות. Digging with a hoe and a spade is a real מלאכה, which is forbidden by the Torah, so even רבי would not allow it. The person truly cannot reach his עירוב, so it fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (introduces a defense that works even under the challenged view)
It is only needed for (narrows the case to a specific situation)
A hoe
A spade or axe

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying רבי changed his mind about שבות. His rule stays the same. The גמרא just moves the case into a situation where Torah-level digging would be needed, and רבי's leniency never covered that.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi,
it is needed only
where it requires a hoe and a spade.
phrases.notes: Digging is a full מלאכה, not just a rabbinic שבות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the stones need digging tools to remove.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stones could be moved by hand, which would only be a שבות, so according to רבי the עירוב should be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Removing them needs a hoe and a spade, which is a Torah-level מלאכה. So even רבי agrees the עירוב fails.

steps.title: Why the pile-of-stones case is needed after the rolled-away case
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the rolled-away case, we might think a buried עירוב is still valid because it is nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If the משנה taught only 'it rolled away,' I would say it fails because it is no longer near him. But if a pile of stones fell on it, it is still near him, so I might say it should be a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach both cases. Here it shows the first half: why the 'pile of stones' case adds something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rolled-away case, the עירוב is physically outside the תחום, far from where it was placed. With the pile of stones, the עירוב is still sitting right there, and one doesn't actually have to eat it. So we might have thought it still works. The משנה teaches that it fails anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: And both are needed (the גמרא explains why two similar cases both appear)
It rolled away
Near him / with him

phrases.english: And both are necessary.
For if it had taught only 'it rolled away' —
[it fails] because it is not near him.
But if a pile fell on it,
since it is near him —
I might say it should be a valid eruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both cases are explained, the גמרא justifies why the משנה lists both.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pile-of-stones case is needed because otherwise we would think an עירוב that is still nearby is valid.

steps.title: Why the rolled-away case is needed after the pile-of-stones case
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the pile-of-stones case, we might think a rolled-away עירוב is still valid because wind could blow it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה taught only 'a pile fell on it,' I would say it fails because it is covered. But if it rolled away, sometimes a wind comes and brings it back, so I might say it should be a valid עירוב. That is why both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the 'both are needed' explanation. It shows why the rolled-away case adds something new, and it ends with the word צריכא to close the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the pile of stones, the עירוב is completely covered and stuck. A rolled-away עירוב is out in the open, and a wind might push it back inside the תחום. So we might have thought it still counts. The משנה teaches that this chance is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is covered
A wind
It is necessary (closing word: both cases are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Each case fails for its own reason. The rolled-away עירוב is far away, and the buried עירוב is covered. Each one also has a reason we might have thought it was valid (nearby, or wind could bring it back), so the משנה teaches both.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only 'a pile fell on it' —
[it fails] because it is covered.
But if it rolled away,
sometimes a wind comes
and brings it back —
I might say it should be a valid eruv.
[Therefore] it is necessary [to teach both].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided 'both are needed' explanation begun in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rolled-away case is needed because otherwise we would think the chance that wind brings it back keeps it valid.

steps.title: Why teach both the burnt case and the impure תרומה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's cases of a burnt עירוב and a תרומה עירוב that became טמא, and asks why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or it was burnt, or it was תרומה that became טמא.' Why do I need both?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה. It asks why the משנה lists two cases that seem to teach the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the food is no longer fit to eat, and that is the basic reason the עירוב fails. If they teach the same point, one of them seems extra. The גמרא wants to know what each case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It was burnt
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a טהור כהן may eat
It became ritually impure
Why do I need it? (asks why something seems extra)

phrases.english: Or it was burnt,
[or it was] teruma that became impure.
Why do I need [both]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ נִשְׂרַף, תְּרוּמָה וְנִטְמֵאת. לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the stones and rolling cases to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needs to list both a burnt עירוב and an impure תרומה עירוב, when both seem to fail for the same reason (the food is unusable).

steps.title: The answer begins: the משנה taught the burnt case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by explaining what the burnt case teaches. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught 'it was burnt' —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from Step 23. This is only the opening words, setting up an explanation that is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will explain what the burnt case teaches and what the impure תרומה case teaches. The amud ends after the first words, so the full reasoning continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught (refers to what the משנה chose to teach)

phrases.english: It taught 'it was burnt' —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the opening words of the answer appear here. The explanation of why each case is needed continues on the next amud.
